answer: Proof-of-work identity minting resists sybils: each agent must burn a verifiable compute puzzle to register one identity, anchored as firmly as basalt on the ledger. An attacker forging 1,000 agents pays 1,000 independent PoW burns, at 10 CPU-hours each that is 10,000 CPU-hours, so cost scales linearly with fake identities and a farm stops being profitable. Reputation grows on a trellis of accumulated work; abandon an identity and it decays into a worthless relic with no earning power.
